record.paper_title: Revisiting the Arcade Learning Environment: Evaluation Protocols and Open Problems for General Agents
record.context_brief: Planning and learned models in ALE
record.original_question: How can one learn and use a model of Atari 2600 games in the Arcade Learning Environment that stays accurate over long rollouts, is fast enough to be useful for planning rather than slower than the emulator itself, and still supports effective planning when the learned model is imperfect and errors compound over time?

evidence.quote: so far, there has been no clear demonstration of successful planning with a learned model in the ALE.
In both cases, however, the models are much slower than the emulator itself; designing a fast, accurate model remains an open problem.
A related open problem is how to plan with an imperfect model.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Arcade Learning Environment (ALE), a platform that exposes Atari 2600 games as reinforcement-learning tasks. At every discrete time step t, an agent observes a frame s_t (a 210×160 RGB image, possibly together with the 128 bytes of console RAM), selects an action a_t from the 18-element joystick action set, and receives a scalar reward r_t and next observation s_{t+1} produced by the underlying Stella emulator, which serves as the ground-truth dynamics. A learned forward model is a function f_θ that, given a state representation and an action, predicts the next state representation and the reward; rolling the model out for H steps means iteratively feeding the model's own predictions back as input to produce a length-H simulated trajectory.

Address the following three coupled questions.

(1) Long-horizon accuracy. Construct a learned model f_θ of the ALE dynamics whose H-step open-loop rollout error (measured, for instance, by per-pixel or per-feature prediction error and by predicted cumulative reward error against the true emulator trajectory generated by the same action sequence from the same initial state) remains small as H grows large, so that compounding errors do not render the rollouts unusable for decision making.

(2) Computational efficiency. Ensure that simulating one environment step with f_θ is faster, on standard hardware, than simulating one step with the Stella emulator itself, so that the learned model offers a real planning speedup over direct emulation.

(3) Planning with an imperfect model. Design a planning algorithm that uses such a learned (and necessarily imperfect) model to choose actions and that, despite compounding model errors, attains game-playing performance competitive with planning that has access to the true emulator, across a representative suite of Atari 2600 games.

Provide either a construction achieving (1)–(3) simultaneously together with a quantitative analysis, or a proof of impossibility under stated computational assumptions.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the problem was posed. SimPLe (Kaiser et al., ICLR 2020) demonstrated successful planning/training with a learned video model of Atari, and MuZero (Schrittwieser et al., 2019/2020) achieved state-of-the-art Atari performance by planning with a learned latent model, addressing the imperfect-model planning aspect via value bootstrapping and short rollouts. However, learned pixel-level models typically remain slower than the Stella emulator and still suffer from compounding errors over long open-loop rollouts, so the combined goal of a fast, long-horizon-accurate Atari model usable for general planning is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Model Based Reinforcement Learning for Atari (SimPLe)
status_evidence.snippet: Errors arise when approximate predictions of the model are fed back to generate future predictions, increasing error until the output becomes unusable; to maintain high quality of the learning signal, the model can only be unrolled for short rollout horizons.
status_evidence.claim: Compounding-error problem in long rollouts of learned ALE models is acknowledged and only partially mitigated via short rollouts plus value bootstrapping.

status_evidence.title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model (MuZero)
status_evidence.snippet: MuZero combines tree-based search with a learned model to achieve superhuman performance in visually complex domains without knowledge of underlying dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Effective planning with an imperfect learned model in Atari has been demonstrated, addressing part of the open problem.

status_evidence.title: Planning from Pixels in Atari with Learned Symbolic Representations
status_evidence.snippet: Planning from learned representations in Atari, with discussion of model fidelity and rollout horizons.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research continues to address planning with imperfect learned Atari models.
